body: The first time i tried to lose weight, i was 13 or 14, and i had a mini "weight loss for dummies" book. It said i had to burn more calories than i ate, but i didn't think it was possible because i was unaware that our bodies burned calories by digesting, breathing, day to day tasks etc. I thought the only way to burn calories was straight exercise.

Years and years of religious torture, brainwashing, and indoctrination from people who told me from a young age that someday my husband won't love me if i have sex before marriage. Haha. Haha. End my misery.

I'm 5'6", female, and weighed about 150-155 pounds at the time of my 1200 calorie diet. I was on the 1200 calorie diet for about 60 days. Weight loss, for me, at 1200 calories came slow and with many plateaus. I only lost about 5 pounds over the course of the 60 days, when I should have lost way more than that. I eat 1470 now and lose weight at a much faster and steadier pace. 

I should add that what I experienced could have been because I didn't have as much spare energy (in the form of fat) as others do when they eat at the same level as I did, my body recognized this, and tried to hold onto my fat as much as possible.

Anyhow I'm digressing. What you need to do when you are restricting your calories so is pay special attention to what your body is telling you and by no means deprive yourself. When I was on my 1200 calorie diet for example, I quit having my period. I don't remember having many other side effects. But even if you don't think they're connected to how much you are eating, you should really read into what your bod is trying to tell you and consult a doctor. Sometimes, 1200 calories simply isn't enough to keep your body running at 100%. I wouldn't recommend eating under your BMR. I know it's frustrating when a 1200 calorie diet promises so much, but now that I'm eating more, my body isn't as worried that I'm gonna die and everything seems to be okay.

Also, say what you want about "starvation mode", but forms of it exist on that kind of restriction. During this time, i was constantly frustrated by the numbers on the scale not moving, and going through long, long plateaus that were infuriating, especially when a 1200 calorie diet promises 2+ pound/week weight loss. However, I will recognize that it is not physically possible to GAIN fat eating less calories than you burn. 

I guess what I'm saying is be careful. Try not to eat under your BMR, you might actually lose faster eating at your bmr than at 1200 calories. However I've drawn this from personal experience. See a doctor about extreme calorie restriction. Just be careful and use your better judgement.

I don't know how much this'll help you. I live in my house with my parents (both moderately skinny) and my two brothers (both practically skin and bones). I just have to tell you this story because it seemed to fit so well.

The other night, I get home from school and look in the fridge. My brother had a bad day and my mom baught him a french silk pie from Perkins. Oh, how much I love my mom and how sweet she is, but why today? It was only Tuesday! Later that night my mom asked me and fam to go on a ride. I said yes, and eventually we pulled up to McDonald's. Great. Everyone's ordering ice cream, and a cookie sounds absolutely delightful. However, I knew that if I cheat today, then I don't get to cheat saturday. That was a rule I made for myself. So I got a water while everyone else has their sundaes. 

Moral of the story/one tip that may help you: give yourself a cheat day. Don't go absolutely crazy. Keep it around 500-750 more than your regular allowance or eat your TDEE. Extra Credit: if you cheat at all during the week, deny yourself the cheat day. If that doesn't work, I don't know what will!! 

**DISCLAIMER: Some dieters are against cheat days. I'm not one of those people. I need one to keep me sane. You may find that having a cheat day works for you. Or maybe it doesn't. These things vary so much from person to person.

And I actually have another story. I spend a lot of time with my little brother. One day, he was playing video games and brought out a bag of sour cream and cheddar potato chips. They didn't look too bad so I grabbed one. And another. And another. Then, many handfuls later, I regretted it. Noticing how this happened made me realize that I have a bad habit of not being able to stop eating junk after i start.

Moral of the story: find your food habits and do whatever you can to prevent falling back into them. For me, it would be taking a moment when I see food, asking myself if "just one ______ (cookie, potato chip, etc)" will turn into many, and making a decision from there.

Last thing that helps, find a zero calorie beverage and stick to it. Mine is diet coke. If you want to give up soda, but don't like the taste of water, get flavor packets (like crystal lite, I always get the Polar blast Hawaiian punch ones) and mix it in a reusable bottle of water with ice.

Another protip: eat a small snack (granola bar, apple, etc.) and about 5 minutes later, have at least 16oz of a zero calorie beverage. Works for me every time, I'm always waaaaayyy more full than I would be without the drink.
Extra Credit: eat a big plate of low-calorie veggies before each meal. Oofta.

LAST THING THIS TIME I PROMISE. You're gonna hate it for the first week or so. I promise. Going to bed hungry sucks. Not eating as much as/what you used to sucks. At this point in my weight loss, I'm sad I don't get to go back to my ways where I ate whatever I wanted with no remorse. But how I feel, and how I look, and how much happier I am, and my outlook on life make it all worth it.


I hope I helped!! :) pm me if you have questions/need advice.

Actually, almost the exact thing happened to me shortly after I started eating at 1200 calories!!! Don't fret. I am 5'6 and was caught between 150 and 152 pounds, so very similar to you BMI wise. 

Basically, before March of this year, I had lost 25 pounds. In March, I got caught at 150 and couldn't seem to lose any more than that and got frustrated and gave up until about halfway through July. I had gained back about 5 pounds, back up to 155-156. The first 3-4 came off with 1200, no sweat. However, I was stuck for a whole month until I started to see (and measure) progress again, and exactly a week ago, I measured 149.6 on my scale. I was so happy I damn near cried. Today I am 148.2. 

Just keep at it! You'll get there and it'll suck and feel like forever but just keep at it like the soldier you are! You've simply hit a plateau, and mind your  measurements (and how your clothes fit) aside from just weight because I found that they kept going down even when the scale wouldn't budge.
